# Sentori

> Self-hosted crash and error reporting for mobile apps, React Native
> first. One Rust binary plus PostgreSQL. Its own wire protocol — it is
> not Sentry-compatible, there is no DSN, and a Sentry SDK cannot talk
> to it.

This file exists because the only thing a developer usually hands an
agent is the instance URL. Everything needed to send a first event is
below; the links are for detail, not for the basics.

## Integrate (React Native)

```
npm install @goliapkg/sentori-react-native
```

```ts
import { sentori } from '@goliapkg/sentori-react-native'

sentori.init({
  token: 'st_…',                       // required — Settings → Tokens, scope `ingest`
  ingestUrl: 'https://your-instance',  // required — the instance root, no path
  release: 'myapp@1.0.0+123',          // optional but needed for symbolication
  environment: __DEV__ ? 'dev' : 'prod',
})
```

Report from code with the verbs. There is no `captureError`, no
`captureException`, no `setUser`, no `startSpan` — if you have seen
those, they are from a pre-v1 page or from Sentry.

```ts
sentori.error(new Error('boom'), { feature: 'checkout' })  // → event id
sentori.warn('slow-checkout', { ms: 1200 })
sentori.trace('cart.opened')
sentori.assert('cart.total-matches', total === expected)
sentori.probe('checkout-double-charge')

sentori.user({ id, email, name })          // or null to clear
sentori.context({ tenant: 'acme' })        // ambient tags on every event
```

Five *kinds* of event (`error`, `warn`, `trace`, `assert`, `probe`);
eight *methods* on `sentori`, the other three being `init`, `user` and
`context`. The package also exports `ErrorBoundary`, `launch`,
`pushSignal`, `registerMaskQuery`, `useTraceNavigation` and
`triggerNativeCrash`.

Every verb returns the event id and never throws: a failure inside
Sentori must never reach the host app.

## Machine-readable

- `GET {instance}/openapi.json` — OpenAPI 3.1, generated from the
  router and served by the server, so its `info.version` is the
  version of the binary answering. Full schemas for `/v1/events`,
  `/v1/events:batch`, `/v1/events/validate` and `/healthz`; every other
  live path is listed with its methods.
- `POST {instance}/v1/events/validate` — **no token required.** Send
  the body you intend to send and it tells you whether ingest would
  parse it. It touches no database, names no project and stores
  nothing.

```
$ curl -sX POST $INSTANCE/v1/events/validate -H 'content-type: application/json' \
    -d '{"kind":"error","occurredAt":"2026-08-27T00:00:00Z","platform":"ios",
         "error":{"message":"x"}}'

{"ok":true,
 "parsed":{"kind":"error","platform":"ios","hasPayload":false,…},
 "ignored":["error"],
 "note":"parsed, but the keys in `ignored` were dropped …"}
```

`ignored` is the useful part: `error` at the top level parses fine and
arrives empty, and nothing else would ever tell you. A body that does
not parse comes back with `field` naming the key — `occurredAt` for the
`timestamp` mistake — so a client can branch on it.

## Send an event without the SDK

```
POST {instance}/v1/events
Authorization: Bearer st_…
Content-Type: application/json
```

```json
{
  "kind": "error",
  "occurredAt": "2026-08-27T00:00:00.000Z",
  "platform": "javascript",
  "release": "myapp@1.0.0+123",
  "environment": "prod",
  "payload": { "error": { "type": "TypeError", "message": "boom" } }
}
```

`kind`, `occurredAt` and `platform` are required. `occurredAt` is
RFC 3339 and has no alias — sending `timestamp` fails with
`422 missing field occurredAt`, and the 422 body is plain text, not
the JSON error shape. Everything else about the event goes inside
`payload`.

Success is `202` with the receipt:

```json
{"eventId":"01a0…","issueId":"01a0…","isNewIssue":true,"regressed":false}
```

`POST {instance}/v1/events:batch` takes `{"events":[…]}`, at most 200.

## Verify it arrived

`issueId` from the `202` is the machine-readable receipt. An
`ingest`-scope token can only write; reading issues back needs a token
with scope `api`, and then `GET {instance}/api/issues`.

## When it fails

Errors are `{"error":"<code>","detail":"…"}`. Branch on `error`;
`detail` and `hint` are prose and change. A `401` carries a `hint`
naming which check failed — wrong prefix, wrong length, unknown token,
or wrong scope. The full generated list is in the error reference
below.

## Probing this instance

The dashboard is a single-page app and its server answers **every**
unknown path with the app's HTML shell and `200`. `/openapi.json`,
`/.well-known/…`, `/docs/anything` all look like they exist. Do not
treat a `200` as proof a resource is there — check the content type,
or that the body is not `<!doctype html>`.

Some paths that are real — not a complete list; `protocol.md` has the
rest, and `/v1/deploys` and the `/v1/push/*` family are also live:

- `GET /healthz` — `{"status":"ok","version":"…",…}`, no auth
- `GET /llms.txt` — this file
- `POST /v1/events`, `POST /v1/events:batch` — ingest
- `GET /api/issues` — read issues, needs an `api`-scope token

A useful asymmetry: the catch-all is GET-only. A mistyped **POST**
fails loudly — `POST /v1/event` answers
`404 {"error":"not_found","detail":"no route for POST /v1/event"}` —
so a wrong ingest path will not silently look like success.

## Docs

- [Getting started](https://github.com/goliajp/sentori/blob/master/docs/getting-started.md): install, first event, and a curl that works
- [React Native quickstart](https://github.com/goliajp/sentori/blob/master/docs/getting-started/react-native.md): the SDK path end to end
- [Protocol reference](https://github.com/goliajp/sentori/blob/master/docs/protocol.md): full wire schema, batching, sourcemap upload, token format
- [Error reference](https://github.com/goliajp/sentori/blob/master/docs/errors.md): every code this server sends, generated from the handlers
- [Self-hosting](https://github.com/goliajp/sentori/blob/master/docs/self-hosting.md): environment variables, backup, restore
- [Troubleshooting](https://github.com/goliajp/sentori/blob/master/docs/troubleshooting.md): the failure modes people actually hit
- [SDK reference](https://github.com/goliajp/sentori/blob/master/sdk/react-native/README.md): the current API surface, including the `init()` options table with defaults. The npm page renders the copy from the last publish, which may lag this one.

## Optional

- [Source maps and native symbols](https://github.com/goliajp/sentori/blob/master/docs/recipes/sourcemap-upload.md): making stacks readable
- [Release versioning](https://github.com/goliajp/sentori/blob/master/docs/recipes/release-versioning.md): what `release` should contain
- [Self-hosted mirror](https://github.com/goliajp/sentori-selfhosted): source to build and run your own instance
- [Archive](https://github.com/goliajp/sentori/tree/master/docs/archive): pages describing versions and features that no longer exist. Do not integrate from these.
